outcome_blind_attestation: no returns, PnL, PF, Sharpe, ranking, backtest or scored metric was computed at any point in this lane; all quantities below are schedule counts, construction rules or worst-case turnover bounds in weight-units

mechanism_family.name: cointegration error-correction relative value (threshold pairs stat-arb)
mechanism_family.distinct_from_lane_partner: A6-P1-OSCOMP (order-size composition) — different signal statistic (two-name log-price spread residual vs sign-agnostic trade-count composition), different counterparty (flow-imbalanced substitute repricing vs attention-driven retail pressure decay), different book shape (weekly threshold pairs vs monthly quintile book)

primary_source_claim.claim: Economic substitutes that are cointegrated share a stationary long-run relation (error-correction representation); a relative-value rule that trades divergence of the spread beyond a threshold and exits on convergence has historically earned spreads robust to conservative execution assumptions, in equities and, with Engle-Granger-type gates and OU-calibrated lookbacks, in cryptocurrency markets.

sources.citation: Engle, R.F., Granger, C.W.J. (1987). Co-Integration and Error Correction: Representation, Estimation, and Testing. Econometrica 55(2), 251-276.
sources.claim_used: cointegration implies an error-correction representation: deviations from the estimated long-run relation are stationary and tend to revert — the theoretical basis for trading the spread residual

sources.citation: Gatev, E., Goetzmann, W.N., Rouwenhorst, K.G. (2006). Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitration Rule. Review of Financial Studies 19(3), 797-827.
sources.claim_used: a pre-formed pairs rule with threshold divergence entry and convergence exit, formed on prior economic grounds (not in-sample performance), earned spreads robust to conservative execution

sources.citation: Avellaneda, M., Lee, J.-H. (2010). Statistical arbitrage in the US equities market. Quantitative Finance 10(7), 761-782.
sources.claim_used: spread mean reversion is calibrated as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process; entry thresholds and holding horizons should be tied to estimated reversion dynamics

sources.citation: Tadi, M., Kortchmeski, I. (2021). Evaluation of Dynamic Cointegration-Based Pairs Trading Strategy in the Cryptocurrency Market. arXiv:2109.10662; also Studies in Economics and Finance.
sources.claim_used: Engle-Granger-type cointegration gates are applicable to crypto pairs; the OU half-life of the spread informs the lookback window; realistic execution (signal-to-fill delay) materially changes outcomes

crypto_perpetual_transfer_caveats: Crypto cointegration is weaker and less persistent than equity cointegration: project-specific news (unlocks, outages, regulatory action) breaks relations. Mitigations: pairs are pre-registered on sector-substitute grounds, the activation gate (trailing Engle-Granger test) is re-run at every stamp, the relation is re-estimated every stamp, and max holding is 8 weeks.

Perpetual funding accrues natively on both legs at mixed 8h/4h/1h cadences and can rival the convergence payoff. Mitigation: funding is charged natively as a cost in every cell and NEVER enters the signal — this is explicitly not a funding-selection family.

In crash regimes cross-correlations jump toward 1 and a leg can collapse idiosyncratically so convergence fails exactly when it matters. Mitigation (partial, acknowledged tail risk): dollar+beta-neutral legs capped at 0.25, hedge-ratio sanity bound, 8-week max holding, weekly stamp re-evaluation; no intraweek stop is possible under the weekly clock and this residual risk is declared, not engineered away.
24/7 markets with weekly decision stamps accept stamp-gap exposure; the weekly clock is a frozen packet constraint and positions are kept small by construction.

economic_mechanism.counterparty: Flow-imbalanced traders: attention or news hitting one substitute leg (one L1, one meme name, one payments asset) while its pre-registered substitutes do not move; the RV desk fading the dislocation is compensated at convergence, with the flow trader paying for immediacy and single-name exposure.
economic_mechanism.expected_sign: Convergence: long the cheap leg, short the rich leg of an activated pair; the spread z-score reverts toward its estimated equilibrium, so the book earns the error-correction term while the pair relation holds.
economic_mechanism.why_persistent_in_perps: Crypto sector clusters are real substitutes with high substitution flow, but retail-driven one-legged attention shocks are frequent; the premium for providing immediate two-legged liquidity on a weekly clock persists because the frozen low-turnover design deliberately leaves the fast convergence margin to faster players and harvests only the slow reversion component.

signal_fields: daily log prices built from completed 15m bars (last close per UTC day) strictly before the stamp
trailing 56d Engle-Granger regression (OLS hedge ratio + residual ADF statistic) recomputed per stamp
rolling 90d daily BTC betas for leg sizing (no BTC leg held)
pit_specification.pit_rule: all estimates use observations with timestamps strictly before the decision stamp (completed bars; no partial tail, no synthesized gaps, per the frozen loader rules); open interest and funding are never signal inputs
pit_specification.availability_clock: pair activatable at Monday 00:00:00Z stamp T iff both legs have complete daily closes for (T-56d, T] and the trailing Engle-Granger residual ADF rejects a unit root at the 10% level with |hedge ratio| in [0.25, 4]; otherwise the pair is dormant for that stamp
pit_specification.execution_lag: one declared lag: fills at the first strictly-later completed 15m event after the stamp (FILLED_NEXT_EVENT); baseline delay 0, stress +1 event (the execution-realism caveat of S7 is why the lag is frozen in the schedule)

universe_and_schedule.universe: the 19 tradeable names (REQUIRED_SYMBOLS minus BTCUSDT); BTCUSDT is benchmark-context-only and never held; pre-registered candidate pairs (same-sector economic substitutes, formed on prior grounds, not performance): (ETH,SOL), (SOL,SUI), (AVAX,NEAR), (ADA,AVAX), (AAVE,LINK), (DOGE,1000PEPE), (1000PEPE,BOME), (XRP,BCH) — all symbols suffixed USDT
universe_and_schedule.eligibility_rule: >=9 eligible names required at every stamp (19 available; newest listing precedes the window); fewer than 9 -> fail-closed carry/flat
universe_and_schedule.decision_clock: every Monday 00:00:00Z, weekly; no intraweek actions ever
universe_and_schedule.formation: trailing 56d daily log prices for the anchor arm; neighbour arm uses max(28d, ceil(2 x estimated OU half-life of the spread))
universe_and_schedule.holding: state-dependent: from entry stamp until the exit condition first holds at a stamp — |z| <= 0.5, or 8 weeks after entry (max holding, exit at that stamp); one state change per pair per 2 consecutive stamps (cooldown)
universe_and_schedule.rebalance_schedule: 52 weekly stamps per 365d (<= 60 floor); entries only when |z| >= 2.0 at a stamp for an activatable pair with capacity

book_construction.shape: threshold pairs book: up to 3 concurrently active pre-registered pairs; each symbol appears in at most one active pair (construction rule, prevents stacking)
book_construction.weight_cap_by_construction: per-pair leg weights are at most +/-0.25 (single-active-pair case: +/-0.20), so every |weight| <= 0.25 <= 0.30 at every stamp by construction
book_construction.pair_sizing: within a pair the leg split satisfies w_A = -(beta_B/beta_B-normalized) sizing such that the beta-weighted net exposure of the two legs is zero (rolling 90d BTC betas, PIT), then normalized to the leg cap
book_construction.beta_neutralisation: portfolio BTC beta is zero by construction at every stamp (sum of beta-weighted leg exposures = 0 per pair); BTC is never held

expected_turnover.cooldown_rule: at most one state change (entry or exit) per pair per 2 consecutive stamps; at most 3 active pairs; worst case <= 78 one-way weight-units per year
expected_turnover.max_symbol_turnover_share_bound: each leg move is a fixed 0.25 (or 0.20) unit; with the 3-pair concurrency cap and the construction rule that a lone active pair runs 0.20 legs, any single symbol's share of one-way turnover is <= 20% <= 25% floor by construction
expected_turnover.base_cost_drag_bound: 78 weight-units/yr worst case x (declared taker rate + 1 adverse tick) stays under the 8%/yr floor at tier-0 floors; expected cadence is far lower because entries require |z| >= 2.0 at a weekly stamp for an activatable pair
expected_turnover.stressed_cost_drag_bound: same bound x (fee x1.5 + 3 adverse ticks) under the 12%/yr floor; a gate FAIL defers the family, never renegotiates a floor

anchor.definition: 56d formation, |z| >= 2.0 entry, |z| <= 0.5 exit or 8-week max holding, 2-week cooldown, up to 3 active pre-registered pairs

neighbour.definition: identical rule except the formation window is max(28d, ceil(2 x estimated OU half-life of the spread)) recomputed per stamp
neighbour.theoretical_justification: Avellaneda-Lee (2010) calibrate spread reversion as an OU process and Tadi-Kortchmeski (2021) derive the crypto lookback window from the OU half-life: a sampling window should be a multiple of the estimated half-life for the equilibrium estimate to be stable — the same mechanism sampled at its theory-matched horizon

causal_negative_control.definition: anchor rule applied to a fixed-seed (20260903) per-stamp random permutation of the pair->symbol assignment across the 19 names (no cluster structure, no pre-registered substitutes), preserving thresholds, book shape, gross, beta-neutralisation and the turnover schedule
causal_negative_control.falsifies_mechanism_if: the randomized-pairing arm matches the anchor under the scored protocol — then the cointegration/substitute structure carries no information and the family is dead (a single-name-reversal renamer could not survive this control, which is precisely the point)
causal_negative_control.non_scored_diagnostics: sign-flipped (fade the wrong way) arm permitted as a diagnostic only; consumes no scored cell

costs_and_stress.fees: declared adapter CostModel floors (tier-0 taker per side, 1 adverse tick floor); arithmetic reused verbatim from GenericStrategyBase.rebalance_cost_between
costs_and_stress.funding: native settlements on BOTH legs while held (LONG_PAYS_POSITIVE_RATE), applied only inside holding spans, mixed 8h/4h/1h cadences consumed natively per symbol (official Binance fundingTime documentation); funding NEVER enters signal, activation or sizing — the family is explicitly not a funding-carry rescue even though spread carry is a real cost/risk
costs_and_stress.stress_cells: frozen surface fee x1.5 / +2 ticks / +1 event delay; family supports the generic six-cell surface (weekly clock has no fold-contract refusal)

falsification_condition: The mechanism is FALSIFIED if any of: (a) the randomized-pairing control matches the anchor under the scored protocol (mechanism carries no information); (b) post-entry spread convergence is indistinguishable from pre-entry drift under a preregistered block-bootstrap sign test at entry stamps; (c) fewer than 2 of the 8 pre-registered pairs are ever activatable across served stamps (no substitution structure in this universe); (d) signal availability < 0.95 of served stamps; (e) any frozen feasibility floor FAILs or is UNAVAILABLE. Scoring is the pipeline's job; this lane computes no outcomes.

ancestry_map.WEEKLY-REVERSAL / MR-RESCUE: DECLARED ADJACENCY, argued distinct: the rejected class is single-name reversal on own past returns; this family's statistic is a two-name cointegration residual with NO own-return term, holding is state-dependent (threshold + max-holding + cooldown) rather than horizon-fixed, and the preregistered mechanism-destroying control (pair randomization) preserves whatever single-name reversal exposure exists while destroying the relative-value structure — the two mechanisms are separable by construction. This lane flags the adjacency transparently for A7-N adjudication and offers NO fallback parameterization if adjudicated a rescue

why_not_a_rescue: This is neither a LOT inversion nor an ILLIQ/OILEV parameter rescue: the family computes no lottery/return-shape statistic, no Amihud-type ratio, and never touches open interest; it seeks no cap raise and no post-score renormalization. Its only adjacency — mean reversion — is at the cross-sectional two-name spread level with an estimated error-correction relation, a mechanism class absent from the forbidden inventory as such, and it is accompanied by a mechanism-destroying control that specifically separates it from any renamed single-name reversal. If A7-N adjudicates it inside the MR-RESCUE class, the family is rejected; no rescue parameterization is offered.
